newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali families in dark over India disaster.
newsitem.headline: Nepali families in dark over India disaster.

text.p: Relatives of the Nepali victims of the world's worst mid-air collision over India were in confusion on Wednesday as they were bombarded with conflicting information, officials said.
The Foreign Ministry said 45 Nepalis were among the some 350 victims of the collision between a Saudi Arabian Airlines Boeing 747 and a Kazakh Ilyushin IL-76 freighter near Delhi on Tuesday.

But Achyut Shrestha of Air Express Private Ltd, general sales agent for Saudi Arabian Airlines in the Himalayan kingdom, said there were 49 Nepali passengers killed in the crash, one of the five worst air disasters.
Shrestha said the 49 included a group of 39 Nepali workers who had been booked on by Gulf Manpower Services, a firm that sends Nepali labourers to Saudi Arabia.
"Relatives are inquiring about the victims but we have not received any confirmation from the concerned airlines," said Megh Lama, an official of the Gulf Manpower Services.
Earlier, a Saudi newspaper said nine Nepalis were among the victims on the Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo.
"We are unable at this moment to confirm how many (Nepali) passengers had actually boarded the aircraft," Shrestha said.
Many Nepali workers, mainly manual labourers, plumbers and drivers, travel to Saudi Arabia and other Gulf countries in search of employment.
Government officials said there were about 8,500 Nepali workers in Saudi Arabia, but analysts said the number could be twice as high because many people went there without informing the government.

Nepal is one of the 10 poorest countries in the world and remittances from workers abroad are a major source of foreign exchange earnings in a country that receives 60 percent of its development budget in foreign aid.
Officials said they did not have records of the amount of money sent home by workers from the Middle East as they did not keep separate records of such transactions.
